title: Spiced Lamb Seekh Kebabs with Mint-Coriander Chutney
summary: Spiced lamb mince is hand-moulded around skewers and grilled until smoky and charred, served with a sharp, fresh mint-coriander chutney.
equipment: 8 flat metal skewers (or thick wooden skewers soaked 2 h)
barbecue or ridged cast-iron griddle pan

ingredients.item: fresh coriander, leaves and tender stems
Kashmiri chilli powder (or 1.5 tsp sweet paprika plus a pinch of cayenne)
fine sea salt or table salt
fresh coriander, leaves and tender stems
fine sea salt or table salt
red onion, very thinly sliced into rings

steps.title: Toast the cumin
steps.text: Toast the cumin seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant, then tip them into a food processor. Toasting wakes up the seeds' oils and gives the kebabs a warmer, more rounded flavour than raw cumin would.

steps.title: Blend the spice paste
steps.text: Add the red onion, fresh coriander, garlic, ginger, green chilli, ground coriander, garam masala, chilli powder, cardamom and salt to the processor and blend to a fine paste.

steps.title: Drain the paste
steps.text: Tip the paste onto a clean tea towel, gather up the edges and squeeze firmly over the sink until no more liquid runs out. A dry paste is essential here; if too much moisture stays in the mix, the kebabs will slide apart on the skewer instead of holding their shape.

steps.title: Mix and chill the lamb
steps.text: Put the lamb mince and the drained paste in a large bowl and knead with your hand for 3-4 minutes until evenly combined and slightly sticky. Cover and chill for at least 1 hour, or up to 24 hours; chilling firms up the fat in the mince, which makes the mixture much easier to shape around a skewer.

steps.title: Make the chutney
steps.text: Blend the mint, coriander, chilli, ginger, lemon juice, sugar, salt and water until smooth, adding a little extra water if needed for a spoonable consistency. Chill until ready to serve.

steps.title: Shape the kebabs
steps.text: With wet hands, divide the lamb mixture into 8 portions. Squeeze each one around a skewer into a sausage shape about 15cm long and 2.5cm thick, pressing firmly along the length so there are no cracks that could fall apart on the grill.

steps.title: Grill until cooked through
steps.text: Heat a barbecue or ridged griddle pan over medium-high heat and brush the kebabs with oil. Grill for 10-12 minutes, turning every 2-3 minutes and only once each side releases easily, until well browned all over and a thermometer in the centre reads 71°C, the safe temperature for minced lamb.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the kebabs with the mint-coriander chutney, sliced red onion rings and lemon wedges on the side. A squeeze of lemon just before eating lifts the warm spicing nicely.

tips: Squeezing the spice paste dry in a tea towel is the single most important step for kebabs that hold together on the skewer.
A common mistake is turning the kebabs too soon; wait until they release easily from the grill or they'll tear apart.
Chilling the lamb mixture before shaping makes it far less sticky and easier to mould.
Wet your hands before shaping to stop the mince sticking to your fingers.
safety: Use a probe thermometer rather than cutting the kebabs open to check doneness, since minced lamb needs to reach 71°C throughout.
storage: Cool any leftover cooked kebabs within 2 hours, refrigerate for up to 2 days, and reheat until piping hot (74°C) before serving; the chutney keeps separately in the fridge for up to 2 days.
